[[File: Elongatedness.png|thumb|right|250px|Elongatedness]]
In [[image processing]], '''elongatedness''' for a region is the ratio between the length and width of the [[minimum bounding rectangle]] of the region. It is considered a [[Feature (computer vision)|feature]] of the region. It can be evaluated as the ratio between the area of the region to its thickness squared:

<math>elongatedness = \frac{length}{width} = \frac{area}{(2 d)^2}</math>.

where the maximum thickness, <math>d</math>, of a holeless region is given by the number of times the region can be [[Erosion (morphology)|eroded]] before disappearing.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.icaen.uiowa.edu/~dip/LECTURE/Shape3.html |title=Shape representation and description: Region-based shape representation and description |access-date=2006-12-26 |archive-date=2011-08-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110817215748/http://www.icaen.uiowa.edu/~dip/LECTURE/Shape3.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
